abstract.text:
A normalizing flow implements two operations: sampling via Equation (1), and evaluating the density via Equation (2). These operations have distinct computational requirements: generating samples and evaluating their density requires only f and its Jacobian determinant, whereas evaluating the density of arbitrary datapoints requires only f −1 and its Jacobian determinant. Thus, the intended usage of the flow dictates whether f, f −1 or both must have efficient implementations. For an overview of various implementations and associated trade-offs, see (Papamakarios et al., 2019).

Normalizing flows are a powerful tool for building expressive distributions in high dimensions. So far, most of the literature has concentrated on learning flows on Euclidean spaces. Some problems however, such as those involving angles, are defined on spaces with more complex geometries, such as tori or spheres. In this paper, we propose and compare expressive and numerically stable flows on such spaces. Our flows are built recursively on the dimension of the space, starting from flows on circles, closed intervals or spheres.

sections.summary: Motivates normalizing flows beyond Euclidean spaces, reviews prior manifold-flow approaches and their limitations, and states the paper's contribution: expressive, numerically stable flows on compact connected manifolds such as circles, tori, and spheres.
sections.title: Introduction, motivation, and contribution

source_span.end_text: 2.2. Generalization to the Torus T D

sections.summary: Develops circle diffeomorphisms satisfying boundary conditions and presents three constructions: Möbius transformations, circular splines, and non-compact projections, including composition, convex combination, invertibility, and expressivity.
sections.title: Flows on the circle S¹

source_span.end_text: 2.3. Generalization to the Sphere S D
source_span.start_text: 2.2. Generalization to the Torus T D

sections.summary: Extends circle flows to tori and products of circles and intervals via autoregressive factorization, periodic conditioners, and coupling or masking.
sections.title: Autoregressive flows on tori and product spaces

source_span.start_text: 2.3. Generalization to the Sphere S D

sections.summary: Constructs sphere flows recursively through cylindrical coordinates, transforming height and base variables, composing T_s→c and T_c→s, and proving the density update despite non-diffeomorphic topology.
sections.title: Recursive flows on spheres via cylindrical coordinates

sections.summary: Explores exponential-map flows using cost-convex scalar fields and the sphere exponential map; introduces a new radial scalar field and notes the O(D³) density-update cost.
sections.title: Exponential-map flows on spheres

sections.summary: Places the work in directional statistics and prior manifold-flow methods: wrapping, projecting, conditioning, mixtures, Lie-group flows, and Gemici et al.'s Riemannian flows.
sections.title: Related work: directional statistics and prior manifold flows

sections.summary: Evaluates flows on T² and S² with KL and ESS, compares NCP, Möbius, and circular splines, and compares recursive sphere flows against polynomial and radial exponential-map flows.
sections.title: Experiments on T² and S²

sections.summary: Compares model classes, discusses practical trade-offs between invertibility and expressivity, and sketches future extensions to SU(D) and U(D) using Euler-angle decompositions.
sections.title: Discussion: comparison, limitations, and future Lie groups

sections.title: References

sections.title: Appendix A–B: density transformations and recursive sphere details

relations.quote: Here, we will show how to adapt the rational-quadratic spline flows of Durkan et al. (2019b) to satisfy the sufficient boundary conditions of circle diffeomorphisms.

relations.quote: Möbius transformations have previously been used to define distributions on the circle and sphere (see e.g. Kato et al., 2008; Wang, 2013; Kato & McCullagh, 2015).

relations.quote: The need for probabilistic modelling of non-Euclidean data often arises in applications where the data is a set of angles, axes or directions (Mardia & Jupp, 2009).

relations.quote: According to the taxonomy of Navarro et al. (2017), directional statistics traditionally uses three approaches for defining distributions on tori and spheres: wrapping, projecting, and conditioning.

sections.summary: Motivates normalizing flows beyond Euclidean spaces, reviews prior manifold-flow approaches and their limitations, and states the paper's contribution: expressive, numerically stable flows on compact connected manifolds such as circles, tori, and spheres.
sections.title: Introduction, motivation, and contribution

sections.summary: Develops circle diffeomorphisms satisfying boundary conditions and presents three constructions: Möbius transformations, circular splines, and non-compact projections, including composition, convex combination, invertibility, and expressivity.

sections.summary: Extends circle flows to tori and products of circles and intervals via autoregressive factorization, periodic conditioners, and coupling or masking.

sections.summary: Constructs sphere flows recursively through cylindrical coordinates, transforming height and base variables, composing T_s→c and T_c→s, and proving the density update despite non-diffeomorphic topology.
sections.title: Recursive flows on spheres via cylindrical coordinates

sections.summary: Explores exponential-map flows using cost-convex scalar fields and the sphere exponential map; introduces a new radial scalar field and notes the O(D³) density-update cost.
sections.title: Exponential-map flows on spheres

sections.summary: Places the work in directional statistics and prior manifold-flow methods: wrapping, projecting, conditioning, mixtures, Lie-group flows, and Gemici et al.'s Riemannian flows.
sections.title: Related work: directional statistics and prior manifold flows

sections.summary: Evaluates flows on T² and S² with KL and ESS, compares NCP, Möbius, and circular splines, and compares recursive sphere flows against polynomial and radial exponential-map flows.
sections.title: Experiments on T² and S²

sections.summary: Compares model classes, discusses practical trade-offs between invertibility and expressivity, and sketches future extensions to SU(D) and U(D) using Euler-angle decompositions.
